description: The figure displays a group of three pie charts representing the problem distribution based on correctness under with and without knowledge settings using the CoT method, categorized by difficulty levels labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard." A shared legend positioned to the right of the charts identifies four categories, each corresponding to a distinct color and representing a slice in each of the three pie charts: N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (light green), N-K- (orange), and N+K- (red). In the "easy" chart, the four slices consist of N-K- at 45.9%, N+K+ at 40.6%, N+K- at 10.1%, and N-K+ at 3.3%. The "medium" chart shows N+K+ at 44.6%, N-K- at 44.3%, N+K- at 7.2%, and N-K+ at 3.9%. Finally, the "hard" chart displays N-K- at 36.8%, N-K+ at 36.2%, N+K+ at 20.1%, and N+K- at 7.0%. Percentage labels are provided directly inside each slice. None of the slices are visually emphasized through exploding, bolding, or offsetting, and the segments do not appear to be ordered in a consistent descending or ascending size sequence across the charts.
